C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No. 270
Date. 22/4/16
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Central Police Station.
Shanghai, April 20, 1916.
REPORT ON Newspaper Report re Ex Military Governor of Chekiang
being Living in Settlement.
Made by D. S. Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
Regarding attached, I beg to report that Tsu Jui (朱瑞)
alias Tsu Cha Zung (朱介人) did reside at No. 126 Chengtu
Road, but Chu Siau Fung (朱晓峰) and his family, who
occupy that house, deny this. Tsu Jui has probably left
for Peking now, for he intended to do so.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D.S.Givens
Detective Sergeant.
Chief Detective Inspector.

刑事调查处
情报登记
第 270 号
日期：1916年4月22日
上海公共租界工部局警务处
中央捕房
上海，1916年4月20日。
关于报纸报道前浙江都督居住于租界内的报告。
由 D. S. Givens 撰写。经首席探长转呈。
阁下，
关于附件，谨此报告，朱瑞（Tsu Jui），又名朱介人（Tsu Cha Zung），曾居住于成都路126号，但现居该处的朱晓峰（Chu Siau Fung）及其家人予以否认。朱瑞可能已按原计划前往北京。
此致，
阁下之恭顺仆人，
D.S.Givens
警佐侦探
首席探长

the first telegram regarding the independence of
Chinkiang was despatched by an employee of the
Chinkiang Telegraph Office who was compelled to do
so by a man named Kang Hyl An 耿義 who was
dressed in foreign clothes and who threatened him
with a pistol. The declaration that Chinkiang had
declared independence was not true and at present
everything was quiet there.

Eastern Times. Magistrate Sun. 沈 of the Chinese city received
a detective report yesterday afternoon saying that the
revolutionists have a secret headquarters at Ern Pine
Lane 二平弄 , inside the new north gate, where are 他 are
plotting to start a rising to-night (Saturday), when
a certain place will be set on fire. The magistrate
promptly transmitted this report to the Chief of Shanghai
and Woosung Police, who sent armed policemen and
detectives to investigate. On their arrival they
found that the revolutionists had escaped with
their belongings.

On the 14th instant Yuan Shih Kai issued a
mandate saying that Chu Yang Kwong 屈映光 , the
Civil Governor of Chekiang has telegraphically
reported that at 4 p.m. on the 11th many militarymen
and people suddenly rushed at the yamen of Chiangchun
Tsu Jui 朱瑞 , whose whereabouts are still unknown.
At that time the said Governor's yamen was protected by
guard. The following day many
military officers and gentry compelled him (Chu)
to become Tutuh, but he would rather die than
accept the offer. After some discussion the officials,
gentry and merchants jointly requested him to continue
in the position of Civil Governor and also act as
Commander-in-Chief of the Chekiang Army in order to
preserve peace and order of that province. This he
consented to do . Peace and order there have now
been restored as usual. Yuan says that the wisdom
of that Governor has brought tranquility to the
whole province of Chekiang. Moreover he has rendered
meritorious service to the country, He is hereby
appointed Acting Chiangchun in charge of military
affairs of Chekiang. Under the present dangerous
circumstances he should do his best for the country
from the beginning to the end. He should at same
time explain to the troops and people to be patriotic
and obey the orders of the Government for which Yuan
continues that he (Yuan) will be grateful.

Tson Hua Sin Pao. Tsu Jui, ex-Chiangchun of Chekiang, took refuge
in a foreign hospital at Hangchow when the proclamation
of independence. Afterwards he left there for Shanghai
by steam-launch under the protection of a foreign
doctor. He arrived here yesterday and is now residing
at the residence of Tsu Hsiao Fung 朱曉鳳 near the corner
of Mandalay and Chengtu Roads. It is said that he is
still communicating with Chu Yang Kwong at Hangchow
through a certain foreigner.

（印：S.M.P. HEAD OFFICE CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION DEPT. I.O 17 APR 1916 M3.）

The Ningpo and Shaoshing military officials have
jointly sent an official despatch to Chu Yang Kwong
asking him to give an answer why he still calls himself
Civil Governor of Chekiang after the declaration of
independence. The Tson Hua Sin Pao strongly criticizes
Chu's traitor like conduct, and other rebel organs in
Frenchtown have advised the citizens of that province
to compel him to retire from his position immediately.

有关镇江独立的第一封电报是由镇江电报局的一名雇员发出的，此人系受一名身穿洋装、名为耿義（Kang Hyl An）的男子持枪胁迫而为之。所谓镇江宣布独立之说并不属实，目前当地一切平静。

《字林西报》。华界沈知事昨日下午接到一份侦探报告，称革命党人在新北门内的二平弄设有一处秘密总部，他们正密谋于今晚（星期六）发动起义，届时将纵火焚烧某处。沈知事随即向上海及吴淞警察总局局长转报了此消息，后者派遣武装巡捕及侦探前往调查。抵达后，他们发现革命党人已携带财物逃离。

本月14日，袁世凯发布命令称，浙江民政长屈映光（Chu Yang Kwong）电报报告，11日下午4时，许多军人和民众突然冲向浙江都督朱瑞（Chiangchun Tsu Jui）的衙门，朱瑞的下落至今不明。当时，该都督衙门有卫兵保护。次日，许多军官和士绅强迫他（屈映光）担任都督，但他宁死不从。经过一番商议，官员、士绅和商人共同请求他继续担任民政长一职，并兼任浙江军队总司令，以维持该省的和平与秩序。他同意了这一请求。目前当地的和平与秩序已恢复正常。袁世凯称，该民政长的智慧为整个浙江省带来了安宁。此外，他对国家有功。兹任命他为代理都督，负责浙江军务。在当前的危险局势下，他应始终为国家尽力。同时，他应向军民解释要爱国并服从政府命令，对此袁世凯表示他将感激不尽。

《中华新报》。浙江前都督朱瑞在宣布独立时避难于杭州的一家外国医院。随后，他在一名外国医生的保护下乘汽艇离开那里前往上海。他于昨日抵达此地，现居住在曼达雷路（Mandalay Road）与成都路转角附近的朱晓凤（Tsu Hsiao Fung）寓所。据说他仍通过某位外国人与在杭州的屈映光保持联系。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处总部 刑事调查处 1916年4月17日 M3。）

宁波和绍兴的军事官员已联合向屈映光发出公函，要求他回答为何在宣布独立后仍自称浙江民政长。《中华新报》强烈批评屈映光的叛徒行径，法租界内的其他反叛报刊也建议该省市民迫使他立即辞职。
